title: Pure relative dimension is preserved by base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix an integer $d\ge0$. If every nonempty fibre of $f$ is pure of dimension $d$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], then for every morphism $S\prime\to S$, the base-changed morphism $f\prime:X\times_S S\prime\to S\prime$ [def-pc-fibre-product] has every nonempty fibre pure of dimension $d$.

proof.text: Let $g:S\prime\to S$ be the chosen base-change morphism and write $f\prime:X\times_S S\prime\to S\prime$ for the second projection. The locally-finite-type base-change lemma gives that $f\prime$ is locally of finite type. For any $s\prime\in S\prime$, put $s=g(s\prime)$. The fibre-dimension-after-base-change lemma identifies $(X\times_S S\prime)_{s\prime}$ with the residue-field base change of $X_s$ and, for every $x\prime$ over $x$, gives $\dim_{x\prime}((X\times_S S\prime)_{s\prime})=\dim_x(X_s)$.

source.place: Tags 01T4 and 02FY, used in the proof of Tag 02NK

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ with nonempty fibre $X_s$. Applying the locally-finite-type base-change lemma to $f$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ makes $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ locally of finite type. The hypothesis and the definition of pure dimension say that every irreducible component of $X_s$ has dimension $d$. The locally-algebraic equidimensional-open lemma, with $Y=O=X_s$ and $n=d$, therefore gives $\dim_x(X_s)=d$ for every $x\in X_s$. (Here the integer $d\ge0$ is viewed as a natural number.)

source.place: Tag 02NK proof, via Tag 02FY and the definition of relative dimension (02NJ)

proof.text: For $s\prime\in S\prime$ and $x\prime\in (X\times_S S\prime)_{s\prime}$, let $x$ be its image in $X$. Then $x\in X_s$ for $s=g(s\prime)$, so this fibre is nonempty and Step 2 applies. Step 1 consequently gives $\dim_{x\prime}((X\times_S S\prime)_{s\prime})=\dim_x(X_s)=d$.

source.place: Tag 02NK proof: the assertion is immediate from Tag 02FY

proof.text: For each $s\prime$, the structure morphism $(X\times_S S\prime)_{s\prime}\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s\prime)$ is locally of finite type by the same base-change lemma. Since a field is locally Noetherian, the locally-finite-type-over-locally-Noetherian lemma makes this fibre locally Noetherian. Apply the constant-local-dimension-components lemma to this fibre as $Y=O$ and $n=d$, using Step 3: every irreducible component has topological Krull dimension $d$. Thus every nonempty fibre of $f\prime$ is pure of dimension $d$; empty fibres satisfy the condition vacuously.
